Real-World QC and Imprinting Analysis: GSE240091 Dataset

Source: vignettes/articles/GSE240091.Rmd
GSE240091.Rmd

Run methylation-array QC and imprintomeR analysis on a public EPIC growing teratoma cohort

Overview

This vignette demonstrates a complete imprintomeR workflow on GSE240091, a public DNA methylation dataset of growing teratoma tissues. Samples are subgrouped by reported growth speed: slow, medium, and rapid. You will:

  1. Download GEO metadata and processed beta values
  2. Prepare raw IDAT metadata for the MethQcSet QC workflow
  3. Run methylation-array QC when IDAT files are available
  4. Create an ImprintomeSet object from QC-clean or processed data
  5. Analyze imprinting status and visualize results
  6. Compare scoring options: DMR type, bootstrap intervals, ICR-balanced and per-ICR scores, and locus panels
  7. Export QC and imprintomeR outputs

GSE240091 uses the Illumina Infinium HumanMethylationEPIC BeadChip (850K/GPL23976). The GEO record includes 12 samples and a raw IDAT archive. The processed-beta route is attempted first when GEO provides matrix values; the raw-IDAT route shows the full QC workflow and is intended for local execution after downloading the supplementary tar file.

Phase 1: Setup & GEO Download

Load libraries 

library(imprintomeR)

if (!requireNamespace("GEOquery", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("GEOquery is required for GEO downloads. Install it with: BiocManager::install(\"GEOquery\")", call. = FALSE)
}
library(GEOquery)
library(tidyverse)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

set.seed(2026)

Download GSE240091 metadata and processed values 

geo_gse <- "GSE240091"
message("Downloading ", geo_gse, " from GEO...")

tryCatch({
  gse <- GEOquery::getGEO(geo_gse, GSEMatrix = TRUE, AnnotGPL = FALSE, getGPL = FALSE)
  eset <- gse[[1]]

  message("Download successful")
  message("  Samples: ", ncol(eset))
  message("  Features: ", nrow(eset))
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Failed to download ", geo_gse, ":\n", conditionMessage(e),
       "\nCheck internet connection and GEO availability.")
})

Extract metadata 

pdata <- pData(eset)

message("Available metadata columns:")
print(colnames(pdata))

message("\nSample overview:")
display_cols <- intersect(
  c("geo_accession", "title", "source_name_ch1", "characteristics_ch1"),
  colnames(pdata)
)
head(pdata[, display_cols, drop = FALSE], n = 6)

Build sample metadata 

sample_title <- if ("title" %in% colnames(pdata)) pdata$title else pdata$geo_accession

# Keep GEO columns that are often useful during interpretation.
optional_cols <- intersect(
  c("source_name_ch1", "characteristics_ch1", "characteristics_ch1.1",
    "characteristics_ch1.2", "characteristics_ch1.3"),
  colnames(pdata)
)

metadata_text <- apply(
  pdata[, intersect(c("title", optional_cols), colnames(pdata)), drop = FALSE],
  1,
  function(z) paste(z, collapse = " ")
)

meta <- data.frame(
  Sample_Name = pdata$geo_accession,
  GEO_Accession = pdata$geo_accession,
  Sample_Title = sample_title,
  Sample_Group = dplyr::case_when(
    grepl("slow", metadata_text, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "GTSslow",
    grepl("medium|mediu[mn]", metadata_text, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "GTSmedium",
    grepl("rapid", metadata_text, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "GTSrapid",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  ),
  Platform = "EPIC",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

meta <- cbind(meta, pdata[, optional_cols, drop = FALSE])

message("Metadata created:")
message("  Samples: ", nrow(meta))
print(table(meta$Sample_Group))
head(meta, n = 6)

Phase 2: Raw IDAT QC Workflow

The raw IDAT archive for GSE240091 is large, so this section is not run by default. Run it locally when you want full preprocessing and QC from raw array files.

Download and unpack supplementary IDAT files 

raw_dir <- file.path("GSE240091_raw")
dir.create(raw_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Downloads GSE240091_RAW.tar from GEO.
supp <- GEOquery::getGEOSuppFiles(geo_gse, makeDirectory = TRUE, baseDir = raw_dir)
print(supp)

tar_file <- rownames(supp)[grepl("RAW\\.tar$", rownames(supp))]
untar(tar_file, exdir = file.path(raw_dir, geo_gse))

# GEO IDAT archives are commonly gzipped inside the tar.
gz_idats <- list.files(
  file.path(raw_dir, geo_gse),
  pattern = "\\.idat\\.gz$",
  recursive = TRUE,
  full.names = TRUE
)
if (length(gz_idats) > 0 && requireNamespace("R.utils", quietly = TRUE)) {
  lapply(gz_idats, R.utils::gunzip, overwrite = TRUE, remove = TRUE)
}

# minfi expects channel suffixes named _Red.idat and _Grn.idat.
# GSE240091 raw files may unpack as lowercase _red.idat and _green.idat.
lowercase_idats <- list.files(
  file.path(raw_dir, geo_gse),
  pattern = "_(red|green)\\.idat$",
  recursive = TRUE,
  full.names = TRUE
)

for (old_file in lowercase_idats) {
  new_file <- sub("_red\\.idat$", "_Red.idat", old_file)
  new_file <- sub("_green\\.idat$", "_Grn.idat", new_file)
  if (!identical(old_file, new_file)) {
    file.rename(old_file, new_file)
  }
}

Create QC-ready metadata with Basename paths

runMethQC() expects a Basename column containing the IDAT path prefix without _Red.idat or _Grn.idat.

idat_files <- list.files(
  file.path(raw_dir, geo_gse),
  pattern = "_(Red|Grn)\\.idat$",
  recursive = TRUE,
  full.names = TRUE
)

# idat_prefixes <- unique(sub("_(red|green)\\.idat(\\.gz)?$", "", idat_files))
idat_prefixes <- unique(sub("_(Red|Grn)\\.idat$", "", idat_files))
idat_base <- basename(idat_prefixes)
idat_map <- data.frame(
  Basename = idat_prefixes,
  GEO_Accession = sub("_.*$", "", idat_base),
  IDAT_Sample_Title = sub("^GSM[0-9]+_?", "", idat_base),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# GEO raw files usually start with GSM accessions. Join by GSM first and keep
# the title-derived name as a readable sample label for QC reports.
meta_qc <- meta %>%
  left_join(idat_map, by = "GEO_Accession") %>%
  mutate(
    Sample_Name = paste(GEO_Accession, "_", IDAT_Sample_Title),
    Sample_Group = Sample_Group,
    Platform = "EPIC"
  )

meta_qc <- meta_qc[, c("Sample_Name", "Sample_Group", "Platform", "Basename")]
head(meta_qc)

Install Bioconductor dependencies if needed

This chunk is disabled by default because it can modify your R library. Enable it when running the raw-IDAT QC workflow in a fresh R or HPC environment. It also refreshes the minfi/matrixStats stack to avoid the useNames = NA is defunct error from incompatible package versions.

required_bioc <- c(
  "minfi",
  "GEOquery",
  "annotate",
  "matrixStats",
  "MatrixGenerics",
  "DelayedMatrixStats",
  "IlluminaHumanMethylationEPICmanifest"
)

missing_bioc <- required_bioc[!vapply(required_bioc, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("BiocManager")
}

if (length(missing_bioc) > 0) {
  BiocManager::install(missing_bioc, ask = FALSE, update = FALSE)
}

# Refresh the packages involved in minfi::detectionP(). This fixes environments
# where an older minfi stack calls matrixStats with the now-defunct useNames = NA.
BiocManager::install(
  c("minfi", "matrixStats", "MatrixGenerics", "DelayedMatrixStats"),
  ask = FALSE,
  update = TRUE
)

Run MethQcSet QC 

library(imprintomeR)
library(minfi)

qcset <- runMethQC(
  meta_qc,
  platform = "EPIC",
  pcutoff = 0.05
)

qc_summary <- qc_summarize(qcset)
str(qc_summary)

qc_matrix <- qc_tables(qcset)[["QC_matrix"]]
message("QC status:")
print(table(qc_matrix$Final.QC))

head(qc_matrix)

QC visualizations 

p_qc_bar <- plot(qcset, type = "qc_bar", outFile = NULL)
print(p_qc_bar)

p_qc_intensity <- plot(qcset, type = "intensity", icutoff = 11, outFile = NULL)
print(p_qc_intensity)

p_qc_detection <- plot(qcset, type = "detection_pval", pcutoff = 0.05, outFile = NULL)
print(p_qc_detection)

p_qc_coverage <- plot(qcset, type = "probe_coverage", outFile = NULL)
print(p_qc_coverage)

p_qc_sex <- plot(qcset, type = "predicted_sex", outFile = NULL)
print(p_qc_sex)

Export QC outputs 

qc_outdir <- "GSE240091_qc_output"
dir.create(qc_outdir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

export(
  qcset,
  outdir = qc_outdir,
  format = c("xlsx", "rds", "txt"),
  prefix = "GSE240091"
)

message("QC outputs exported to: ", qc_outdir)

Phase 3: Prepare Beta Values for ImprintomeSet

Use QC-clean beta values when available

If you ran the raw-IDAT QC workflow above, use PASS samples from qcset.

qcset_pass <- subsetMethQC(qcset, final_qc = "PASS")

message("QC-clean samples: ", ncol(beta(qcset_pass)))
head(meta(qcset_pass))

saveRDS(qcset_pass, file = file.path(qc_outdir, "GSE240091_qcset_pass.rds"))

x <- as.ImprintomeSet(
  qcset_pass,
  probeset = readRDS(system.file("extdata", "probesets_hg38.rds", package = "imprintomeR"))[["selected"]],
  genome = "hg38"
)

Phase 4: Run Workflow & Compute Statistics

Execute imprintomeR analysis 

message("Running imprintome analysis...")
x <- runImprintome(x, probeset = "selected", ids_cutoff = 0.2)
message("Analysis complete")

res <- results(x)
message("Results available:")
print(names(res))

status <- res[["AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected"]]
head(status, n = 5)

Compute per-group statistics 

message("Imprinting status by group:")
print(table(status[, c("Sample_Group", "Mechanism")]))

stat_summary <- status %>%
  group_by(Sample_Group, Mechanism) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    n = n(),
    median_IDS = median(IDS, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_Angle = median(Angle, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Sample_Group, desc(n))

stat_summary

Review key metrics 

message("IDS distribution:")
print(summary(status$IDS))

message("\nMechanism classification:")
print(table(status$Mechanism))

message("\nAngle distribution:")
print(summary(status$Angle))

Phase 6: Results Interpretation

Summary statistics 

normal_n <- sum(status$Mechanism == "NORMAL", na.rm = TRUE)
total_n <- nrow(status)
normal_pct <- normal_n / total_n * 100
abnormal_pct <- 100 - normal_pct

message("=== OVERALL IMPRINTING SUMMARY ===")
message(sprintf("Normal imprinting:   %6.1f%% (%d/%d samples)",
                normal_pct, normal_n, total_n))
message(sprintf("Altered imprinting:  %6.1f%% (%d/%d samples)",
                abnormal_pct, total_n - normal_n, total_n))

message("\n=== BY SAMPLE GROUP ===")
for (group in unique(status$Sample_Group)) {
  idx <- status$Sample_Group == group
  n <- sum(idx)
  normal <- sum(status$Mechanism[idx] == "NORMAL", na.rm = TRUE)
  message(sprintf("%12s: %d samples, %d normal (%.1f%%)",
                  group, n, normal, 100 * normal / n))
}

Identify samples with aberrant imprinting 

abnormal <- status %>% filter(Mechanism != "NORMAL")
sample_col <- intersect(c("Sample_Name", "Sample_ID"), colnames(status))[1]

if (nrow(abnormal) > 0) {
  message("=== ABERRANT IMPRINTING SAMPLES ===")
  message("Sample count: ", nrow(abnormal))
  print(abnormal %>% select(all_of(sample_col), Sample_Group, Mechanism, IDS, Angle) %>% head(n = 12))
} else {
  message("All samples show normal imprinting patterns by the selected IDS cutoff.")
}

Key findings template 

message("=== KEY BIOLOGICAL INSIGHTS TEMPLATE ===")
message("1. Dataset: GSE240091, growing teratoma tissue methylation cohort")
message("2. Platform: Illumina HumanMethylationEPIC / 850K")
message("3. Samples analyzed: ", nrow(status))
message("4. IDS range: [",
        round(min(status$IDS, na.rm = TRUE), 3), ", ",
        round(max(status$IDS, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "]")
message("5. Most common mechanism: ",
        names(sort(table(status$Mechanism), decreasing = TRUE))[1])
message("6. Use growth_summary and detailed_status to compare imprinting metrics across growth-speed groups.")

Phase 7: Scoring Options

The sections above use the package defaults: the selected panel scored on gametic ICRs against the fixed 0.5 reference. This phase shows the other scoring options on the same data. Each call adds a result table to results(x) under its own name, so earlier results are kept.

GSE240091 contains growing teratoma samples only, with no control group, so all scores here use the fixed 0.5 reference.

Gametic ICRs, all probes and secondary DMRs

runImprintome() scores the core selected panel on gametic ICRs by default (dmr_type = "gametic"). dmr_type = "all" scores every probe, as in earlier package versions, and dmr_type = "secondary" scores the secondary DMRs separately.

x <- runImprintome(x, probeset = "selected", dmr_type = "all")
x <- runImprintome(x, probeset = "selected", dmr_type = "secondary")
res <- results(x)

scored <- c(gametic    = "AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected",
            all_probes = "AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected.all",
            secondary  = "AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected.secondary")

# Probes per parental class for each selection
t(sapply(scored, function(nm) unlist(res[[nm]][1, c("n_paternal_probes", "n_maternal_probes")])))

# Mechanism of each sample under each selection
mechanism_by_selection <- data.frame(
  Sample_Name  = status$Sample_Name,
  Sample_Group = status$Sample_Group,
  sapply(scored, function(nm) res[[nm]]$Mechanism[match(status$Sample_Name, res[[nm]]$Sample_Name)])
)
mechanism_by_selection[order(mechanism_by_selection$Sample_Group), ]

The gametic paternal class is essentially the H19/IGF2 IG-DMR, so report n_paternal_probes alongside gametic scores.

Bootstrap uncertainty intervals

n_boot adds percentile intervals for IDS and Angle from a two-stage bootstrap (ICRs, then probes within ICRs), and Mechanism_support, the fraction of replicates that fall in the reported sector. Use at least 1,000 replicates for reporting; 200 keep this example fast.

x <- runImprintome(x, probeset = "selected", n_boot = 200, seed = 2026,
                   result_name = "AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected.boot")
boot <- results(x)[["AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected.boot"]]
boot[, c("Sample_Name", "Sample_Group", "IDS", "IDS_lower", "IDS_upper",
         "Angle", "Angle_lower", "Angle_upper", "Mechanism", "Mechanism_support")]

The intervals are conditional on the reference (with in-cohort controls, resample_reference = TRUE includes its uncertainty). The origin permutation test (n_perm) is interpretable only for scores centred on control samples (reference_group), and CalibrateIDS() needs tissue-matched controls, so neither is shown here.

ICR-balanced IDS and per-ICR calls

The sample-level IDS pools all probes of a parental class, so probe-rich ICRs dominate it. balance = "icr" takes the median within each ICR and then across ICRs, so that each ICR counts once. icr = TRUE also scores each ICR on its own and summarizes the altered ICRs per sample.

x <- runImprintome(x, probeset = "selected", balance = "icr", icr = TRUE)
res <- results(x)

# Probe-pooled versus ICR-balanced IDS
balanced <- res[["AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected.icr"]]
data.frame(Sample_Name      = status$Sample_Name,
           Sample_Group     = status$Sample_Group,
           IDS_pooled       = status$IDS,
           IDS_icr_balanced = balanced$IDS[match(status$Sample_Name, balanced$Sample_Name)])

# Per-ICR table (one row per sample and ICR) and per-sample summary
icr_table   <- res[["ICRStatus.selected"]]
icr_summary <- res[["ICRSummary.selected"]]
table(icr_table$DMR_type[!duplicated(icr_table$ICR_name)])   # ICRs scored, by DMR type
icr_summary[, c("Sample_Name", "Sample_Group", "n_icrs", "n_altered", "n_gain", "n_loss",
                "n_altered_chromosomes", "MLID")]

# Count gametic ICRs only
SummarizeICRStatus(icr_table, dmr_type = "gametic")[, c("Sample_Name", "n_icrs", "n_altered", "MLID")]

Per-ICR calls cover all annotated ICRs, secondary DMRs included. The call thresholds (|deviation| ≥ 0.175 and |z| ≥ 2) were selected and evaluated with control samples. GSE240091 has no control samples. Without controls, z is unavailable and only the deviation criterion applies, so tissue-specific methylation is called altered. All five teratoma samples have 24–36 altered ICRs and are flagged multi-locus; without controls these calls mix imprinting changes with tumour- and tissue-specific methylation. Treat these calls as exploratory, or rerun with controls from the same study (reference_group), or with a larger delta_cutoff such as 0.25.

Locus panels: chr11p15 and chr20q13 (GNAS)

Locus panels give a two-axis IDS/Angle for a single imprinted domain: IC1 and IC2 at 11p15.5 (chr11p15), and GNAS-NESP against the maternal GNAS DMRs at 20q13 (chr20q13).

x <- runImprintome(x, probeset = "chr11p15")
x <- runImprintome(x, probeset = "chr20q13")
res <- results(x)

do.call(rbind, lapply(c("chr11p15", "chr20q13"), function(p) {
  res[[paste0("AnalyzeImprintStatus.", p)]] %>%
    group_by(Sample_Group) %>%
    summarise(panel = p, n = n(), median_IDS = round(median(IDS), 3), max_IDS = round(max(IDS), 3),
              .groups = "drop")
}))

Per-ICR heatmap

The icr_heatmap plot type draws the stored per-ICR table, samples by ICRs; non-gametic ICRs are marked with *. runImprintomeVisualizations() includes it in the default set whenever runImprintome(..., icr = TRUE) has been run.

x <- runImprintomeVisualizations(
  x,
  plot_types = "icr_heatmap",
  probeset = "selected",
  prefix = "GSE240091_icr_heatmap",
  store_plots = TRUE,
  save_plots = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)
options(repr.plot.width = 12, repr.plot.height = 5)
print(plots(x)[["icr_heatmap.selected"]])
names(results(x))

Phase 8: Export Results

  outdir = "GSE240091_imprintome_output",
  prefix = "GSE240091",
  save_plots = TRUE,
  plot_device = "pdf",
  overwrite = TRUE
)

head(manifest)

export() writes the full ImprintomeSet object as <prefix>_imprintomeSet.rds, plus results(x) and optionally plots(x). Save extra summary tables only when you need custom reporting beyond the export manifest.

Jupyter Notebook Conversion Guide

A run copy of this guide as a notebook, with outputs, is tutorials/GSE240091.ipynb. This guide is plain Markdown (code blocks are shown, not run, on the website); each R code block is one notebook cell. To create a notebook with an R kernel:

jupytext --from md --to notebook --set-kernel ir vignettes/articles/GSE240091.Rmd

Tips for Jupyter users: - Run the raw-IDAT download and QC cells only when you need full preprocessing; they download a large archive. - Save the downloaded GEO and IDAT files once and reuse them, rather than downloading in every session. - Set outFile in plot calls to save publication-ready PDFs or PNGs. - End with local({ si <- sessionInfo(); si$BLAS <- basename(si$BLAS); si$LAPACK <- basename(si$LAPACK); si }) so that saved notebooks do not record local library paths.
